C1.why: He said مفتوح ('open') to mean relaxed. Amal said 'No. You're a key', and he switched to مرتاح.

C2.why: He dropped من and said شغلت بيتي. Amal answered 'صح، من بيتي', and he repeated من بيتي.

C3.why: He put el- on آخر (الآخر اجتماعتي). Amal asked 'Did you add (el)?', and he fixed it to آخر.

C4.why: He used the plural اجتماعاتي for a single meeting. Amal said 'It's one. اجتماع.'

C5.why: He put the feminine الأخيرة on the masculine اجتماع. Amal said 'No, اجتماع is masculine, you don't need a t', and he fixed it to الأخير.

C6.why: He said على واحدة without el-. Amal recast it as الوحدة, and he repeated it.

C7.why: He said خمس in the date. Amal said 'Mm. No', and he fixed it to خمسة; she then asked about the a-ending.

C8.why: He checked the meaning of هذي الفترة in English; that is a comprehension check, not a mistake in Arabic.

C9.why: He said خمس for the temperature. Amal said 'No. مش خمس'; this is a new corrected moment after the date.

C10.why: He said ستة عشر (16) where he meant sixty. Amal reacted 'Wow' and typed 5amse u sitteen in chat.

C11.why: This was a question testing the rule ('can I use بادات'), not a real attempt to say something.

C12.why: Repeating her example, he said the masculine form with el-. Amal said 'No. صعبة', and his reply shows he had said the masculine.

C13.why: This is the same moment as C12; it is counted there.

C14.why: This was a question about the rule, and Amal said كبيرات and other forms are also acceptable.

C15.why: He said behkesh. Amal recast it as بحكيش and explained that the long vowel is kept.

C16.why: He gave the verb for 'miss' when asked for 'complain'. Amal said 'That's I don't miss', and he retried.

C17.why: He dropped the you-form t in the negative command. Amal said 'Where's the t? You keep the t.'

C18.why: This belongs to the same repair of the same word as C17, so C17 counts it.

C19.why: After being fixed, he dropped the t again (enzaigish). Amal said 'لا، it doesn't work. تنزعجش', so it counts as a repeat slip.

C20.why: He used هيك اشي for 'anything else'. Amal pointed out that it means 'something like this', and he retried; her chat shows ay ishi.

C21.why: He left the -ish off the negated verb (matenbisti). Amal said 'No. Where's your ish?'

C22.why: After her first fix, he left off -ish again. Amal asked 'Where's your ish?' a second time, so it is a repeat slip.

C23.why: Her 'Zia.' is unclear, she then accepted his 'ziyad' with 'Mm-hmm', and the difference may be pronunciation or a speech-to-text error.

C24.why: He said in basatish / in basatetish. Amal recast it as Inbastatish several times and told him to add ma.
